bundle.author: hhkarimi
bundle.title: [DATA-2627] Combine the voter file and L2 consumer-only people into gp_api_people
bundle.body:
Gives gp-api one people table for Michigan that covers both registered voters and the people who appear only in the L2 commercial file. Ticket: [DATA-2627](https://app.clickup.com/t/17tnw2b40rm).

## What changed

- **`gp_api_people`** (new view): every `gp_api_voters` row, plus every row of `gp_api_consumer_only_people`. Columns, in order:
  - the `gp_api_voters` columns
  - `Registered_Voter`: true for voter-file rows
  - `District_Source`: `voter_file` for voter-file rows
  - the commercial-only columns from `gp_api_commercial_people`, null on voter-file rows
- **`gp_api_consumer_only_people`** (new table): commercial-file people with no matching `LALVOTERID` anywhere in the national voter file, using the same columns. It's a table so that the anti-join and the district lookup run once per build, not on every app query.
  - `id` is the voter file's salted hash of `LALVOTERID` when the person has one (566k people whose ID has left the voter file), otherwise a salted hash of `Individual_Id`. Both are UUIDs, as gp-api requires.
  - Voter-file columns (party, turnout, registration, `Voter_Status`, scores) are null.
  - District columns and `Precinct` are placed by area (below). Where no area matches, County and the state legislative and congressional districts fall back to the commercial file's own values.
- **`int__l2_area_district_profiles`** (new table): for each ZIP+4, census block, block group and tract in a state with a commercial file, the most common complete set of district values (every `get_l2_district_types()` column, plus `Precinct`) among the voters there.
- **`assert_gp_api_consumer_only_people_ids_not_voter_ids`**: no consumer-only ID matches a voter ID. Testing uniqueness on the 220M-row view would be expensive, so the test runs on the table.

## Why it's shaped this way

- **The whole district set comes from one group of voters**, rather than taking the most common value of each column separately. That keeps the columns consistent with each other: a ward always belongs to its city. The values are the voter file's raw strings, so gp-api's district filter (`<district column> = <district name>`) matches them exactly.
- **ZIP+4 comes first, then block, block group, tract.** To compare, I placed matched voters using their commercial-file address and checked the result against their voter-file districts:

  | Matched voters with both a ZIP+4 and a block in the map | All 230 district columns match |
  |---|---|
  | Placed by ZIP+4 | 94.2% |
  | Placed by census block | 93.6% |

  Single columns match about 96% of the time (State House: 96.2% by ZIP+4, 96.0% by block). Part of the gap is people whose commercial address differs from their voter address.
- **Union columns are listed by name, not position**, so a change to the voter table's columns can't shift values into the wrong columns.
- **The Michigan total is high (11.3M).** The commercial file holds everyone L2 links to the state through transactions, including people who also transact in other states. The vendor has confirmed this.

## Verification (dev, `dbt_hugh`)

- `dbt build` on the three models and the singular test: 23 pass.
- Michigan rows in `gp_api_people`: 8,047,596 from the voter file and 3,228,030 consumer-only. No duplicate IDs.
- Where consumer-only districts came from:

  | Source | Rows |
  |---|---|
  | ZIP+4 | 3,065,408 |
  | Census block | 84,285 |
  | Block group | 5,994 |
  | Tract | 122 |
  | No match | 72,221 (2.2%) |

- Share of voters in an area who have its most common full set (district columns plus Precinct): ZIP+4 99.0%, block 97.7%, block group 80.3%, tract 61.1%.
- The share of rows with City and Township filled is about the same for consumer-only rows as for voter rows (49%/49% vs 46%/54%).

diff --git a/dbt/project/models/intermediate/l2/int__l2_area_district_profiles.sql b/dbt/project/models/intermediate/l2/int__l2_area_district_profiles.sql
new file mode 100644
index 0000000..19530b5
--- /dev/null
+++ b/dbt/project/models/intermediate/l2/int__l2_area_district_profiles.sql
@@ -0,0 +1,95 @@
+{{ config(materialized="table") }}
+
+-- The most common full set of L2 district values (and precinct) among voters in each
+-- small area,
+-- for placing people who are not in the voter file. Taking the whole set from one
+-- group of voters, rather than the most common value per column, keeps the columns
+-- consistent with each other (a ward always belongs to its city). Values are the
+-- voter file's raw strings, so they match gp_api_voters and the district table.
+-- Built only for states with a commercial file.
+{% set district_types = get_l2_district_types() + ["Precinct"] %}
+
+with
+    commercial_states as (
+        select distinct state
+        from {{ ref("stg_l2_commercial__l2_commercial_20260912_mi") }}
+        where state is not null
+    ),
+
+    voters as (
+        select
+            -- L2 stores the block geocode as a number, dropping leading zeros.
+            lpad(
+                cast(residence_addresses_complete_census_geocode as string), 15, '0'
+            ) as block_geoid,
+            concat(
+                residence_addresses_zip, '-', residence_addresses_zipplus4
+            ) as zip_plus_4,
+            -- Blanks are nulled to match how m_people_api__voter serves them.
+            named_struct(
+                {%- for c in district_types %}
+                    '{{ c }}',
+                    nullif(cast(`{{ c }}` as string), '')
+                    {%- if not loop.last %},{% endif %}
+                {%- endfor %}
+            ) as districts
+        from {{ ref("int__l2_nationwide_uniform") }}
+        where state_postal_code in (select state from commercial_states)
+    ),
+
+    profiled as (select *, sha2(to_json(districts), 256) as profile_id from voters),
+
+    areas as (
+        select 'census_block' as area_type, block_geoid as area_id, profile_id
+        from profiled
+        where block_geoid is not null
+        union all
+        select 'census_block_group', left(block_geoid, 12), profile_id
+        from profiled
+        where block_geoid is not null
+        union all
+        select 'census_tract', left(block_geoid, 11), profile_id
+        from profiled
+        where block_geoid is not null
+        union all
+        select 'zip_plus_4', zip_plus_4, profile_id
+        from profiled
+        where zip_plus_4 is not null
+    ),
+
+    profile_counts as (
+        select area_type, area_id, profile_id, count(*) as voters_with_profile
+        from areas
+        group by area_type, area_id, profile_id
+    ),
+
+    modal as (
+        select
+            *,
+            sum(voters_with_profile) over (
+                partition by area_type, area_id
+            ) as voters_in_area
+        from profile_counts
+        qualify
+            row_number() over (
+                partition by area_type, area_id
+                order by voters_with_profile desc, profile_id
+            )
+            = 1
+    ),
+
+    profiles as (
+        select profile_id, any_value(districts) as districts
+        from profiled
+        group by profile_id
+    )
+
+select
+    modal.area_type,
+    modal.area_id,
+    modal.voters_in_area,
+    modal.voters_with_profile,
+    modal.voters_with_profile / modal.voters_in_area as profile_share,
+    profiles.districts.*
+from modal
+inner join profiles on modal.profile_id = profiles.profile_id

index a119f66..68f92d9 100644
--- a/dbt/project/models/marts/gp_api/_gp_api__models.yml
+++ b/dbt/project/models/marts/gp_api/_gp_api__models.yml
@@ -29,6 +29,83 @@ models:
               arguments:
                 min_value: 18
 
+  - name: gp_api_consumer_only_people
+    description: >
+      People in the L2 commercial file who are not in gp_api_voters, in the
+      gp_api_voters column contract so gp_api_people can union the two.
+      Voter-file columns (party, turnout history, registration, scores) are
+      null. District columns and Precinct come as one set from the most common
+      values among voters in the person's ZIP+4, else census block, block group
+      or tract (int__l2_area_district_profiles). Where no area matches, County
+      and the state legislative and congressional districts fall back to the
+      commercial file's own values. The commercial-only columns of
+      gp_api_commercial_people follow.
+    columns:
+      - name: id
+        description: >
+          The voter-file id (salted hash of LALVOTERID, as in gp_api_voters)
+          when the person has a LALVOTERID that is no longer in the voter file,
+          otherwise a salted hash of individual_id.
+        data_tests:
+          - unique
+          - not_null
+          - is_uuid
+      - name: individual_id
+        data_tests:
+          - unique
+          - not_null
+      - name: LALVOTERID
+        data_tests:
+          - unique
+      - name: Registered_Voter
+        description: Always false; the row is not in the voter file.
+        data_tests:
+          - not_null
+          - accepted_values:
+              arguments:
+                values: [false]
+      - name: District_Source
+        description: >
+          The area whose voters supplied the district columns. Null when no area
+          matched.
+        data_tests:
+          - accepted_values:
+              arguments:
+                values:
+                  - zip_plus_4
+                  - census_block
+                  - census_block_group
+                  - census_tract
+      - name: geocode_full
+        description: >
+          The commercial file's 15-digit census block GEOID, joined as-is to the
+          area profiles' zero-padded ids. The file arrives as text, so leading
+          zeros survive, unlike the voter file's numeric geocode. The test fails
+          the build if a file ever drops them, rather than padding silently.
+        data_tests:
+          - dbt_expectations.expect_column_values_to_match_regex:
+              arguments:
+                regex: "^[0-9]{15}$"
+
+  - name: gp_api_people
+    description: >
+      Everyone the app can reach: every gp_api_voters row plus the people in
+      gp_api_consumer_only_people. Columns are those of gp_api_voters, then
+      Registered_Voter and District_Source, then the commercial-only columns,
+      which are null on voter rows. The commercial file holds everyone L2 links
+      to the state through transactions, including people who also transact
+      elsewhere, so the total exceeds the state's adult population.
+      ids do not collide across the two halves, which
+      assert_gp_api_consumer_only_people_ids_not_voter_ids checks on the table
+      rather than on this large view.
+    columns:
+      - name: Registered_Voter
+        description: True when the row comes from the voter file.
+      - name: District_Source
+        description: >
+          voter_file for voter rows; for consumer-only rows, the area whose
+          voters supplied the district columns, or null when none matched.
+
   - name: gp_api_districts
     description: Pass-through of m_people_api__district
 
diff --git a/dbt/project/models/marts/gp_api/gp_api_consumer_only_people.sql b/dbt/project/models/marts/gp_api/gp_api_consumer_only_people.sql
new file mode 100644
index 0000000..f6bf206
--- /dev/null
+++ b/dbt/project/models/marts/gp_api/gp_api_consumer_only_people.sql
@@ -0,0 +1,120 @@
+{#- A table, so the anti-join against the nationwide voter file and the district
+    lookup run once per build instead of on every app query. -#}
+{{ config(materialized="table", auto_liquid_cluster=True) }}
+
+{%- set voter_columns = adapter.get_columns_in_relation(ref("gp_api_voters")) -%}
+{%- set voter_names = voter_columns | map(attribute="name") | map("lower") | list -%}
+{%- set commercial_relation_columns = adapter.get_columns_in_relation(
+    ref("gp_api_commercial_people")
+) -%}
+{%- set commercial_columns = (
+    commercial_relation_columns
+    | map(attribute="name")
+    | map("lower")
+    | list
+) -%}
+{#- Precinct is placed by area like the districts, so the precinct filter
+    reaches these people too. -#}
+{%- set district_types = (
+    (get_l2_district_types() + ["Precinct"]) | map("lower") | list
+) %}
+
+with
+    voters as (select `LALVOTERID` from {{ ref("gp_api_voters") }}),
+
+    -- Anti-joined on the whole voter file rather than one state, so an id taken
+    -- from LALVOTERID below can never repeat a voter row's id.
+    consumer_only as (
+        select
+            commercial.*,
+            concat(
+                commercial.`Residence_Addresses_Zip`,
+                '-',
+                commercial.`Residence_Addresses_ZipPlus4`
+            ) as zip_plus_4
+        from {{ ref("gp_api_commercial_people") }} as commercial
+        left anti join voters on commercial.`LALVOTERID` = voters.`LALVOTERID`
+    ),
+
+    profiles as (select * from {{ ref("int__l2_area_district_profiles") }}),
+
+    -- Every district column comes from one area, so the set stays consistent.
+    -- ZIP+4 goes first: placing voters by their own commercial address, it
+    -- reproduces their voter-file districts slightly more often than the block.
+    area_choice as (
+        select
+            consumer_only.individual_id,
+            coalesce(
+                zip4.area_type, block.area_type, block_group.area_type, tract.area_type
+            ) as area_type,
+            coalesce(
+                zip4.area_id, block.area_id, block_group.area_id, tract.area_id
+            ) as area_id
+        from consumer_only
+        left join
+            profiles as zip4
+            on zip4.area_type = 'zip_plus_4'
+            and consumer_only.zip_plus_4 = zip4.area_id
+        left join
+            profiles as block
+            on block.area_type = 'census_block'
+            and consumer_only.geocode_full = block.area_id
+        left join
+            profiles as block_group
+            on block_group.area_type = 'census_block_group'
+            and left(consumer_only.geocode_full, 12) = block_group.area_id
+        left join
+            profiles as tract
+            on tract.area_type = 'census_tract'
+            and left(consumer_only.geocode_full, 11) = tract.area_id
+    )
+
+select
+    {%- for column in voter_columns %}
+        {%- set name = column.name %}
+        {%- if name | lower == "id" %}
+            {#- generate_salted_uuid hashes a null input to a fixed value, so the
+                branch has to be explicit rather than a coalesce. #}
+            case
+                when consumer_only.`LALVOTERID` is not null
+                then
+                    {{
+                        generate_salted_uuid(
+                            fields=["consumer_only.`LALVOTERID`"], salt="l2"
+                        )
+                    }}
+                else
+                    {{
+                        generate_salted_uuid(
+                            fields=["consumer_only.individual_id"],
+                            salt="l2_commercial",
+                        )
+                    }}
+            end as id,
+        {%- elif name | lower in district_types and name | lower in commercial_columns %}
+            {#- The commercial file's own value fills in only where no area
+                matched, so it never mixes into an area's set. #}
+            cast(
+                coalesce(
+                    profiles.`{{ name }}`, consumer_only.`{{ name }}`
+                ) as {{ column.dtype }}
+            ) as `{{ name }}`,
+        {%- elif name | lower in district_types %}
+            cast(profiles.`{{ name }}` as {{ column.dtype }}) as `{{ name }}`,
+        {%- elif name | lower in commercial_columns %}
+            cast(consumer_only.`{{ name }}` as {{ column.dtype }}) as `{{ name }}`,
+        {%- else %} cast(null as {{ column.dtype }}) as `{{ name }}`,
+        {%- endif %}
+    {%- endfor %}
+    false as `Registered_Voter`,
+    area_choice.area_type as `District_Source`,
+    {%- for column in commercial_relation_columns
+        if column.name | lower not in voter_names %}
+        consumer_only.`{{ column.name }}`{% if not loop.last %},{% endif %}
+    {%- endfor %}
+from consumer_only
+inner join area_choice on consumer_only.individual_id = area_choice.individual_id
+left join
+    profiles
+    on area_choice.area_type = profiles.area_type
+    and area_choice.area_id = profiles.area_id
diff --git a/dbt/project/models/marts/gp_api/gp_api_people.sql b/dbt/project/models/marts/gp_api/gp_api_people.sql
new file mode 100644
index 0000000..eb0aef4
--- /dev/null
+++ b/dbt/project/models/marts/gp_api/gp_api_people.sql
@@ -0,0 +1,35 @@
+{#- Columns are listed by name on both sides: a positional union would silently
+    shift values if the two column orders ever drifted apart. -#}
+{%- set voter_columns = adapter.get_columns_in_relation(ref("gp_api_voters")) -%}
+{%- set voter_names = voter_columns | map(attribute="name") | map("lower") | list -%}
+{%- set flag_names = ["registered_voter", "district_source"] -%}
+{#- The commercial file's own columns, filled only on consumer-only rows. -#}
+{%- set commercial_columns = [] -%}
+{%- for column in adapter.get_columns_in_relation(
+    ref("gp_api_consumer_only_people")
+) -%}
+    {%- if column.name | lower not in voter_names + flag_names -%}
+        {%- do commercial_columns.append(column) -%}
+    {%- endif -%}
+{%- endfor %}
+
+select
+    {%- for column in voter_columns %} `{{ column.name }}`,{% endfor %}
+    true as `Registered_Voter`,
+    'voter_file' as `District_Source`,
+    {%- for column in commercial_columns %}
+        cast(null as {{ column.dtype }}) as `{{ column.name }}`
+        {%- if not loop.last %},{% endif %}
+    {%- endfor %}
+from {{ ref("gp_api_voters") }}
+
+union all
+
+select
+    {%- for column in voter_columns %} `{{ column.name }}`,{% endfor %}
+    `Registered_Voter`,
+    `District_Source`,
+    {%- for column in commercial_columns %}
+        `{{ column.name }}`{% if not loop.last %},{% endif %}
+    {%- endfor %}
+from {{ ref("gp_api_consumer_only_people") }}
diff --git a/dbt/project/tests/assert_gp_api_consumer_only_people_ids_not_voter_ids.sql b/dbt/project/tests/assert_gp_api_consumer_only_people_ids_not_voter_ids.sql
new file mode 100644
index 0000000..aa31c4f
--- /dev/null
+++ b/dbt/project/tests/assert_gp_api_consumer_only_people_ids_not_voter_ids.sql
@@ -0,0 +1,5 @@
+-- gp_api_people unions the two, so a shared id would make it non-unique. An id
+-- taken from LALVOTERID collides only if the anti-join missed a voter.
+select consumer_only.id
+from {{ ref("gp_api_consumer_only_people") }} as consumer_only
+inner join {{ ref("gp_api_voters") }} as voters on consumer_only.id = voters.id

priorFindings.body:
**Latent geocode leading-zero mismatch on census-block joins.**

`int__l2_area_district_profiles` zero-pads `block_geoid` to 15 characters via `lpad(cast(residence_addresses_complete_census_geocode as string), 15, '0')`, but here `consumer_only.geocode_full` is used raw (no `lpad`). The voter-file comment in the profiles model confirms L2 stores block geocodes as numbers with leading zeros stripped. No upstream `lpad` is applied to `geocode_full` anywhere in the staging or intermediate layer (confirmed by grep). Currently only Michigan (FIPS 26) is loaded so no leading zero exists and the join works, but the moment a state with FIPS 01–09 (Alabama through Connecticut) is added, all census-block, block-group, and tract join legs will silently fail, pushing those people to the no-match path with null districts.

Falsification check: grepped the full codebase for any `lpad` on `geocode_full` — none found. The only scenario that would disprove this is if L2 pre-pads the commercial export, but the voter-file comment explicitly warns of the opposite pattern from the same vendor.

findings.body:
**ZIP+4 suffix leading-zero mismatch silently breaks the highest-priority area join.**

`residence_addresses_zipplus4` is sourced as `INT` (confirmed in `l2_column_classification.csv`), so when the Python model `cast_identifier_columns_to_string` casts it to STRING, a value like `0123` has already been stored as `123`. The `concat` here produces e.g. `'48104-123'`.

On the commercial side, `Zip4` is classified as a string in the staging model and preserves the leading zero, so `gp_api_consumer_only_people.sql` concatenates it as `'48104-0123'`.

The join at `gp_api_consumer_only_people.sql` line 57 (`consumer_only.zip_plus_4 = zip4.area_id`) compares `'48104-0123'` against `'48104-123'` — these never match. Any consumer-only person whose USPS ZIP+4 suffix begins with `0` silently misses the ZIP+4 area match and falls through to the coarser block/block-group/tract lookups, producing degraded or no district assignment.

Falsification check: this would be disproved by an `lpad` on the voter-side suffix before the `concat`, or evidence the source stores the column as STRING. Neither is present: the source schema shows INT, the staging is a pass-through, and `cast_identifier_columns_to_string` does not re-pad.
findings.suggestion:
concat(
    residence_addresses_zip,
    '-',
    lpad(cast(residence_addresses_zipplus4 as string), 4, '0')
) as zip_plus_4,

output.summary: This PR adds three new dbt models to combine voter-file and L2 commercial-only people into a single `gp_api_people` view for Michigan, with district assignment via area profiles keyed on ZIP+4, census block, block group, and tract. The scout flagged five areas: a ZIP+4 leading-zero format mismatch between voter and commercial sides, a hardcoded single-state staging ref, commercial fallback district formatting, test sufficiency for union uniqueness, and a potential division-by-zero. Deep review confirmed one blocker: the voter file stores `ZipPlus4` as INT (losing leading zeros), while the commercial file preserves them as strings, so the ZIP+4 join — the highest-priority area match — silently fails for any suffix starting with 0. The other four leads were falsified: the single-state ref matches the project-wide pattern, commercial district values are already normalized to voter-file format, the combination of uniqueness and cross-table tests guarantees union uniqueness, and `voters_in_area` is structurally ≥ 1. The prior finding about geocode leading-zero mismatch has been mitigated by a new regex data test (`^[0-9]{15}$`) that fails the build if the commercial file ever arrives without 15-digit geocodes. The human reviewer should confirm that the `lpad` fix for the ZIP+4 suffix is applied consistently wherever voter-side zip_plus_4 is constructed.

findings.body:
**ZIP+4 suffix leading-zero mismatch silently breaks the highest-priority area join.**

`residence_addresses_zipplus4` is sourced as `INT` (confirmed in `l2_column_classification.csv`), so when the Python model `cast_identifier_columns_to_string` casts it to STRING, a value like `0123` has already been stored as `123`. The `concat` here produces e.g. `'48104-123'`.

On the commercial side, `Zip4` is classified as a string in the staging model and preserves the leading zero, so `gp_api_consumer_only_people.sql` concatenates it as `'48104-0123'`.

The join at `gp_api_consumer_only_people.sql` line 57 (`consumer_only.zip_plus_4 = zip4.area_id`) compares `'48104-0123'` against `'48104-123'` — these never match. Any consumer-only person whose USPS ZIP+4 suffix begins with `0` silently misses the ZIP+4 area match and falls through to the coarser block/block-group/tract lookups, producing degraded or no district assignment.

Falsification check: this would be disproved by an `lpad` on the voter-side suffix before the `concat`, or evidence the source stores the column as STRING. Neither is present: the source schema shows INT, the staging is a pass-through, and `cast_identifier_columns_to_string` does not re-pad.
findings.suggestion:
concat(
    residence_addresses_zip,
    '-',
    lpad(cast(residence_addresses_zipplus4 as string), 4, '0')
) as zip_plus_4,
